issue.title: sase_questions skill source case mismatch: "your turn ends as DONE" vs test expects "Your turn ends"
issue.description: tests/main/test_init_skills_sources.py::test_shipped_skill_source_is_discoverable_for_all_skill_providers[sase_questions-expected_phrases11] expects the exact-case phrase "Your turn ends as `DONE`" inside the sase_questions skill source body, but the shipped skill source (rendered from src/sase/xprompts/skills/) contains it lowercase: "...Otherwise, your turn ends as `DONE`; there is nothing after this for you to do." The test's collapse_whitespace comparison is case-sensitive, so this substring check fails deterministically. Fix is either capitalizing 'Your' in the skill source prose, or lowercasing the expected_phrases tuple entry in the test. Discovered on 2026-09-16 while verifying an unrelated gate-reclaim change (plans/202609/accepted_gate_reclaim.md) via 'just check'; the escalated full-suite run failed only this one node. Reproduced independently on a clean master checkout (git stash -u, rerun, git stash pop) with zero other changes applied, so this predates and is unrelated to the gate-reclaim work.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic exact-case substring mismatch between static skill markdown prose and a static test expected_phrases tuple entry -- neither side is randomized, parallelism-dependent, or order-dependent. Reproduced twice: once inside the just check full-suite escalation, and once again in isolation on a clean git-stash-restored master HEAD 7636fe03b8 with none of the unrelated gate-reclaim diff applied.
